events.title: St. Francis hears the call to apostolic life
events.shortBlurb: At a little chapel near Assisi the young Francis heard the Gospel of the mission and resolved to live it to the letter…
body: On 24 February 1208, the feast of St. Matthias, Francis of Assisi heard Mass at the Portiuncula, the little chapel of St. Mary of the Angels below Assisi that he had helped to rebuild. Born in 1181 or 1182, the son of a rich cloth merchant, he had already renounced his inheritance and was living as a penitent among the lepers and ruined churches of the valley.

The Gospel told of Christ sending the Twelve to preach the kingdom of God with neither gold nor silver, nor scrip, nor two coats, nor shoes, nor staff. Francis took the words as spoken to himself, crying, 'This is what I wish, this is what I seek, this is what I long to do with all my heart,' and casting off shoes and staff girded his tunic with a cord.

He began to preach penance and peace in the streets of Assisi, and companions soon joined him, first Bernard of Quintavalle and then Peter of Cattani, so that the little brotherhood took shape. The next year Francis led them to Rome, where Pope Innocent III gave spoken approval to their way of life, the beginning of the Order of Friars Minor.

sources.text: Thomas of Celano, First Life of St. Francis (public-domain translation)
